idiom_name: module-level functions over a duck-typed object (+ Protocol for the declared requirement)
implementation_notes: Python has no method injection, so the servant is a module-level function taking the serviced object (move_to(shape, position)) - the same shape the standard library uses for behaviour that does not belong to the type (copy.copy, heapq.heapify, bisect.insort) - or a small stateless helper object when the behaviour needs configuration. The capability the servant requires is duck-typed: it uses the attributes it needs, optionally declared for static checkers with a typing.Protocol. When the serviced classes can inherit, abstract base classes ship mixin methods that provide the behaviour once the class supplies the primitives (collections.abc.Set needs only __contains__, __iter__ and __len__ and supplies the rest), and functools.singledispatch turns the same idea into a function that dispatches on the serviced object's type without any shared base class.
pitfalls: Duck typing defers the contract to runtime: a servant that assumes shape.position raises AttributeError deep inside the call - declare the requirement (Protocol, ABC) or validate at the module boundary.
singledispatch selects on the exact class and its MRO, not on structural checks: a subclass that is not registered silently falls back to a base or default implementation.
Functions are the easy option, but a module full of unrelated helpers becomes the same grab-bag as a Java Utils class - split by service and keep the serviced-object assumption in the signature.
sources: Python documentation, functools - singledispatch/singledispatchmethod: dispatch on the type of the first argument, MRO/ABC resolution and registration; https://docs.python.org/3/library/functools.html

Python documentation, collections.abc - ABCs usable as mixins that supply the full API from a few abstract primitives (Set needs __contains__, __iter__, __len__), the inheritance-based realisation of the same idea; https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html

faif/python-patterns, patterns/behavioral/servant.py - a Python servant class over unrelated serviced classes, referencing the same catalogue description; https://github.com/faif/python-patterns/blob/master/patterns/behavioral/servant.py
